This document will detail the derivations required for the MLEs of all of the tensor variate distributions.

## Tensor Variate Skewed Distribution

In the tensor variate case, the normal variance mean mixture model is an efficient way to introduce skewness. A random tensor $\tensor{X}$ can be written as

$$\tensor{X}_{i} = \tensor{M} + W_{i} \tensor{A} + \sqrt{W_{i}} \tensor{V}_{i}$$

where $\tensor{M}$ is a location tensor, $\tensor{A}$ is a skewness tensor, $\tensor{V} \sim \mathcal{N}_{n^*}(\mathbb{O}, \bigotimes_{d=1}^{D} \Sigma_{d})$ and $W > 0$ is a positive random variable. The distribution of $\tensor{X}$ will depend on the distribution of $W$.


We are interested in obtaining the MLEs of the distribution $X$. 

If we knew the latent values $W_{i}$, then the distribution of $X_{i}$ would be normal.

$$X_{i} | W_{i} = w_{i} \sim N_{p}(W_{i} A, W_{i} \otimes_{i=1}^k \Sigma_{k})$$

Let the distribution of $w$ be represented as $h(w)$. Then the joint density can be written as

$$f(X_{i}, W_{i}; \theta) = f(X_{i}|w_{i}) f(w_{i}).$$

Thus, we can represent the joint distribution as a product of the tensor variate normal PDF and the PDF of $W$.
